Sunlight appears white but is actually composed of all colors of the visible spectrum, each traveling at a different wavelength. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions, with shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) scattering far more than longer ones (red and orange) due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
